improvementsForA: Replace the pseudo-glyph rules text with real, legible typography: every face-up card (hand fan, board creatures, the 8/12/18 card) carries decorative scribble marks instead of words, which instantly reads as unfinished concept art the moment a player looks down.

Pull back the global warm bloom/haze: the yellow wash flattens contrast across the entire midfield, overexposes the top-left corner (fence and brook dissolve into milky blur), and makes the whole render feel like it is behind frosted glass.

Resolve the detail crops at asset level: the corner-tl fence posts smear into mush, and the corner-bl foreground mass is ambiguous between a boulder and a bush at 2x; these need crisper edges and clearer material identity.
Fix the corner-tr canopy material: the sunlit tree crown reads semi-transparent where the light overlay sits on the low-poly geometry, so the tree looks ghosted instead of solid.
Strengthen the empty card-slot outlines: under the haze the faint white rectangles nearly vanish, so the playable zones on both rows are hard to read at a glance.

Unify the card frame color script: the teal-framed wisp cards jump out of the otherwise gold/parchment system; either motivate the teal as a faction color with supporting accents or bring the frames back to the warm palette.
improvementsForB: The play surface is a flat mustard poster, not a meadow: add painted value variation, grass tufting, warm/cool patches, and dappled shadows cast from the perimeter trees so the board reads as ground rather than a UI backdrop.

Perimeter vegetation is placeholder-grade: the trees, bushes, and rocks are untextured low-poly blobs in near-uniform dark green with almost no shading gradient or contact shadow into the field (corner-tr and corner-bl are especially empty and unfinished).
The river reads as a glowing neon-cyan ribbon with an outer glow, like a UI path, not water; give it banks, depth, foam, and sun-consistent specular instead of emissive glow.

Commit to a single sun: cards drop crisp shadows to the lower-right but the scenery is lit flat/ambient, so the world and the cards do not share one light; add long warm directional shadows from every tree, rock, and fence post.

The center divider is a perfectly straight flat line with a flat diamond sitting on top of the ground; let its glow fall off onto the grass, add slight organic waver, and let scene shadows interact with it so it exists in the world.
Card fronts are pure flat vector: add subtle paper grain, edge wear, and a lighting response (soft top-light gradient) so the very readable card design also feels like a physical object in the scene.
notes: A reads as a painted place: one warm low sun, long integrated shadows, a brook, fence, flowers, and grass texture under every card, with card stacks that visibly sink into the scene. B is far more readable (real card names and rules text, crisp edge thickness, clean shadows) but its world is a flat mustard board with placeholder low-poly blobs and a neon river, so it never reads as scenery. A's failures are finishing failures (fake glyph text, heavy bloom, blurry corners); B's failures are foundational environment-art failures, which is why A sweeps every crop and takes the overall.
